title: Terms Clause: The Share of Unused Premium Returned Where Claims Have Been Settled
content:
Where coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans is given up after benefit has been drawn on it, only a share of the unused premium comes back, and which share turns on what stands on the plan in the window the coverage counts claims over, being the 12 whole months to the handling date.

Where a settlement entry stands on the plan inside that window and the benefit drawn in that window is at or above 0.5 of the coverage's yearly benefit allowance, 0.5 of the unused premium is returned. Where a settlement entry stands on the plan inside that window and the benefit drawn in it is below that share of the yearly benefit allowance, 0.75 of the unused premium is returned. In any other case the whole of the unused premium is returned.

## What the claims record gives

| Settlement entries inside the 12 whole months | Benefit drawn in that window | Share of the unused premium returned |
|---|---|---|
| one or more | at or above 0.5 of the coverage's yearly benefit allowance | 0.5 |
| one or more | below 0.5 of that allowance | 0.75 |
| none | (not reached) | the whole of it |

## The yearly benefit allowance each plan sets

| Plan | Yearly benefit allowance |
|---|---|
| Manufacturer Limited Warranty | 350.00 USD |
| Belrose Care Plan 2-Year | 1200.00 USD |
| Belrose Care Plan 3-Year | 2500.00 USD |
| Belrose Care Plan 5-Year | 5000.00 USD |
| Belrose Lifetime Care Plan | 12000.00 USD |
| Belrose Heirloom Protection Plan | 40000.00 USD |

## Boundary readings

On a plan whose yearly benefit allowance is 2500.00 USD, benefit of exactly 1250.00 USD drawn inside the window stands at 0.5 of that allowance, so the first reading is taken and 0.5 of the unused premium is returned. Benefit of 1249.99 USD drawn inside the window stands below it, so 0.75 of the unused premium is returned. Where no settlement entry stands inside the window at all, the whole of the unused premium is returned however much benefit was drawn before it.
